Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final pricing exhibit annotations & ask re: cap/floor language

Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our annotated Pricing Exhibit (Redwood_Pricing_Exhibit_v2_marked.pdf) plus a short change log. Two asks from our side to keep the doc moving: 

1) Can you confirm CloudMed’s tolerance on a temporary floor true-up window? On the call you mentioned a 60-day operational buffer; we want that reflected as a soft window (no automatic penalty) vs. a hard true-up.

2) We flagged places where “billable tokens” is referenced but not defined (see §2.1 and §5.3). Please confirm whether CloudMed will accept the Redwood definition (tokens billed per request-response pair, excluding cached prefixes) or propose an alternate definition.

Quick notes in the attachment: 
- Proposed concession: if monthly billed tokens exceed 150% of committed monthly average for three consecutive months, Redwood will apply a temporary surcharge for the following month rather than an immediate contract true-up.
- Request clarification on the cap floor trigger (we highlighted different thresholds for burst vs sustained).

If you can send a marked copy back with CloudMed legal’s comments we’ll do an internal redline and try to get to final language this week. I’ve CC’d Marissa and Karthik for pricing/legal ops alignment.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Exhibit_v2_marked.pdf (pdf), summarized-change-log.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the pdf and call summary. Attaching CloudMed's redline (CloudMed_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). A few quick responses inline: 

- True-up window: procurement prefers a 45-day operational buffer with a discrete remediation step after 90 days for sustained overshoot. They will not accept a fully open "soft" window without remediation.
- Billable tokens: legal flagged that CloudMed needs explicit exclusion language for internal QA/test traffic and for tokens generated by third-party telemetry (we've noted suggested language).
- Cap/floor triggers: we proposed a tiered approach where burst (single-month >200%) triggers a surcharge only; sustained (>150% for 3 months) triggers a contract-level true-up.

Tom (cc) will follow up on the specific wording for auditability and metrics (what counts as an "invoiceable token").

Please review our edits and either accept in-place or propose alternate wording — we can take the redline into negotiation on Friday.

Attachments: CloudMed_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (docx)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: CloudMed redline — position suggestions before legal call

Team — forwarding CloudMed's redline. Key points for us before Tom's legal reply: 

- Procurement wants a 45-day buffer + remediation step at 90 days. I think we can accept 45 days but push to 60 for operational reasons (deploy lag, metric reconciliation).
- They insist on excluding QA/test traffic from billable tokens. We should accept that but tighten the required tagging/headers on dev traffic so it's auditable.
- CloudMed's tiered trigger for burst vs sustained is reasonable but their remedy language lets them unilaterally declare "sustained" without ops-level evidence. We should require a joint reconciliation step and a mutually agreed metric feed (we can propose Redwood's token-export CSV format).

Suggested asks for legal: 
1) Keep 60-day operational buffer but add an explicit joint reconciliation step within 30 days after the buffer.
2) Define billable tokens with an explicit exclusion list and require CloudMed to provide a data export for any contested months.
3) Accept a surcharge for single-month bursts >200% but cap surcharge at 20% for that month.

Attaching summarized-change-log.xlsx with our proposed trade-offs. Happy to take the call with CloudMed legal if we need to negotiate language live.

Best,
Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: CloudMed redline — position suggestions before legal call

Jordan / team —

I've pulled a short excerpt we can propose as counter-language for the order form (text below). This is intended to be tight, machine-auditable, and symmetric.

--- proposed excerpt (for §5.3, caps & true-ups) ---
"Billable Tokens" means tokens generated by Customer requests to Redwood's inference API that result in a model compute invocation, excluding tokens identified in Customer-tagged environments (dev|qa|staging), and excluding tokens returned from cache hits per §3.2. For any disputed period, Customer shall provide a token export in Redwood CSV schema within 14 days of Redwood's request; Redwood will provide a reconciliation report within 7 days thereafter.

Trigger definitions:
- Burst surcharge: A single monthly period where billable tokens >200% of the committed monthly average triggers a surcharge equal to min(20% of that month's charges, prorated by overage).
- Sustained true-up: Any rolling 90-day window where average monthly billable tokens >150% of committed monthly average triggers a joint reconciliation. If joint reconciliation confirms sustained overshoot, parties will negotiate an order form amendment reflective of new usage banding.

--- end excerpt ---

Two operational asks: extend the joint reconciliation window to 45 days post-trigger (gives ops team time to produce exports) and require a single-data-source assertion in the CSV export (we already capture request_id and timestamp which will help).

If everyone is comfortable I can drop this into the next doc pass and produce an in-place redline for the call.

Karthik
Head of Pricing & Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@cloudmed.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 18:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final pricing exhibit annotations & ask re: cap/floor language

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the suggested excerpt; legal reviewed and we have a narrow counter and a path to sign: 

1) CloudMed will accept the proposed "Billable Tokens" definition with the following clarifying edits: add explicit language that tokens generated by third-party integrations are considered billable unless tagged as non-prod by the Customer.
2) We can accept a 60-day operational buffer only if Redwood accepts a 30-day joint reconciliation window (CloudMed prefers that reconciliation begins within 30 days and is concluded within 60 days of notification).
3) We will accept the burst surcharge cap at 20% but request Redwood waive the surcharge for the first single-month burst that occurs during the first 6 months post-go-live.

Final conditional for DocuSign: CloudMed legal needs an explicit audit-log retention commitment of 12 months for request-level logs related to billing disputes. If Redwood can confirm 12-month retention and provide the token-export CSV within 14 days of a dispute notice, CloudMed is prepared to execute the order form.

I've attached our final mark (CloudMed_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). If Redwood accepts the audit-log retention and the waived first-burst concession, please confirm and we'll circulate a DocuSign envelope (link below).
